messages:
maria: quick kickoff question 1 what should our default behavior be when the intake bench shows a regression: immediate rejection or put model into a monitored probation?
aj: immediate rejection keeps bad builds out fast, but benches are noisy. a monitored probation offers signal from real traffic.
sanjay: we've had false positives from microtokenizer diffs earlier. probation helped catch that in canary.
maria: ok but how long is probation? we can't let it drag and consume infra credits.
aj: propose short probation (3h) for small models and extended (48h) for large/enterprise ones. run golden probes plus 0.5% canary traffic during probation.
elaine: thresholds matter. 2% mismatch on golden probes isn't the same as a user-visible regression. we need smoothing and context.
sanjay: idea: combine metrics into a composite acceptance score. e.g. 35% golden-probe delta, 30% p95 latency regression, 25% token throughput, 10% human eval. pass if >= 0.75.
maria: who tunes those weights? ML infra or SRE?
aj: ML infra to provide model-family defaults; SRE/ops can override per-customer.
elaine: operationally, we need explicit rollback rules during probation: e.g., error rate > 0.2% OR p95 +100ms => auto-rollback. and immediate fail on infra-critical errors (OOM, serialization exception).
sanjay: to implement rollback quickly we need a canary circuit breaker that can instantly drop the new variant from dedicated pools.
maria: implementation sketch: intake -> bench smoke -> if checks pass -> create probation entry in registry with metadata {duration, canary_pct, required_score, budget}. probation agent aggregates metrics and updates score; gate service makes final pass/fail.
aj: big question: bench results vary with quantization and batching. we should bench the most-likely production variants (fp16, q4, single/multi-shard) but avoid full Cartesian product. prioritize by deployment profile.
sanjay: agreed. define a bench-matrix priority list per model-family to trim combos.
maria: also enforce a probation budget cap, default 4 GPU-hours, owner can request more with approval. prevents runaway cost.
elaine: telemetry: mark probation runs so they don't contaminate production baselines and show a single probation report in Console listing pass/fail reasons + diffs.
aj: Console UX: show which probe(s) contributed most to score, sample failing inputs, and stack traces for kernel-level failures. make it explorable.
sanjay: edgecase: a model that consistently fails golden probes but improves user satisfaction for a customer. allow manual override with two approvers and a documented risk plan.
maria: manual overrides must create an audit entry and require a post-deploy regression plan.
elaine: after probation success, do a 24h A/B roll with incremental ramp before full production. reduces surprises.
aj: summary: fail-fast on infra-critical errors; otherwise probation with composite scorer + staged A/B rollout. I'll write an RFC describing state machine, probation metadata and gate API.
noah-bot: created probation-ticket PB-9876: model repo/edge-chat, duration: 48h, canary:0.5%
maria: please include onboarding checklist items: bench priority matrix, budget cap, rollback triggers, manual-override flow.
elaine: and include a logging contract for kernel errors (OOM, dtype mismatch) so bench failures are actionable.
sanjay: I'll start a prototype of the scorer service and post a link to the repo later this week.
aj: great 1 ping here when it's up and we'll iterate on the weights after some runs.
maria: thanks all, feels like a clear next step.
